about: When input happened, as React receives it (sample/TimingProbe.tsx; input.h's eventTime; docs/native-foundation.mdx, protocol version 3): each input event carries when its device registered it (time_ns, CLOCK_MONOTONIC: libinput's time on a session, the director's paced time here), and React gets it as the W3C pointer event's timeStamp and the touch's timestamp, as Android's events carry a MotionEvent's eventTime. Two presses 300 ms apart by their device's time are a double press though the application's JavaScript held the thread for 600 ms between them (the second arrives behind it); two 600 ms apart are not. Before, every event carried when the host got round to it: the first pair was taken for two single presses.

steps.name: two presses 300 ms apart, JavaScript busy for 600 ms after the first: a double press

texts: Pair 1: 300 ms apart (touch 300 ms), double press: yes, handled at least 600 ms apart

steps.name: two presses 600 ms apart: two single presses

texts: Pair 2: 600 ms apart (touch 600 ms), double press: no, handled at least 600 ms apart
